record.provider: SourceForge File Release System (FRS) + project web space

free_tier.stated: NO PUBLISHED QUOTA. The Service Quotas page says verbatim: 'There are currently no fixed capacity limits around usage of our services. In lieu of specific disk usage caps (quotas), we may contact projects if they are using significant storage.' It then gives a soft expectation rather than a cap: 'Keep disk usage to a reasonable level: 5GB or less is ideal. 20-30GB may be permissible. (limits may vary and be flexible depending on the situation)'. So the real number is 20-30 GB of tolerated storage per project, soft, and multiplied by unlimited projects per account.

That is the hard number and it is published. retention: indefinite - download stats are keyed to path+filename and files are never pruned for age; but the docs warn 'Users are responsible for backing up all of their files

egress.terms: Free and genuinely CDN'd: 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' (create page) plus 'a geographically-distributed network of mirror servers, which receive copies of the files and dispense them to users'. No billing relationship anywhere. Downloads 302 to a geo-selected mirror (zenlayer.dl.sourceforge.net from this vantage) and are served by nginx.

record.tooling: Native sftp/scp/rsync-over-ssh, no wrapper needed. FRS host `frs.sourceforge.net` path `/home/frs/project/PROJECT_UNIX_NAME/`; web host `web.sourceforge.net` path `/home/project-web/PROJECT_UNIX_NAME/htdocs`. SFTP is batch-scriptable with key auth ('Use key-based authentication, since password entry can't safely be automated'). rsync is the documented path for anything over 100 MB because it resumes. Read side has machine APIs: `/projects/<name>/best_release.json` (JSON with bytes/md5sum), `/projects/<name>/rss?path=/` (per-file size in `files:size`), and `downloads.sourceforge.net/project/...`.
record.chaining: Each account can register unlimited projects ('you automatically are given administrator rights for that particular project'; the only gate is ODF-compliant OSS licensing + a one-time phone/SMS PIN). At the tolerated 20-30 GB/project that is 20-30 GB x N projects x N accounts. The real find is that the number is NEGOTIABLE and unpublished - 'If you are planning to do something which consumes huge amounts of disk, please ask first' - so the ceiling is a support ticket, not a wall. Two independent storage surfaces per project (FRS + project web htdocs), plus git/hg/svn repos, plus wiki/ticket attachments.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: 'Individual files larger than 10 GB will not replicate out to our mirrors and can not be downloaded.' That is the hard number and it is published. retention: indefinite - download stats are keyed to path+filename and files are never pruned for age; but the docs warn 'Users are responsible for backing up all of their files. SourceForge.net will not restore individual files.' request-rate: none published; the docs instead route large uploads to rsync for resume. Filename charset is restricted (no & : % ? / * $, may not start with space or dot).
record.reliability_note: The only fragile part is the soft quota: 20-30 GB 'may be permissible' means a project that grows to hundreds of GB gets an email, not a hard stop - enforcement is discretionary. SFTP is reachable and live (banner SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.4 on port 22). One structural caution: the FRS host deliberately does not list the project directory over SFTP ('your project directory is available, even if you cannot see it listed'), so clients must use absolute paths and cannot enumerate.
record.confidence_note: The absence of a fixed cap is stated on the page as re-read. Was reported; now documented.

free_tier.stated: No fixed quota. SourceForge's own docs: 'There are currently no fixed capacity limits around usage of our services. In lieu of specific disk usage caps (quotas), we may contact projects if they are using significant storage.' Guidance: '5GB or less is ideal. 20-30GB may be permissible (limits may vary and be flexible depending on the situation)'. So ~20-30 GB per project as a practical band, with no hard number.

retention.stated: SourceForge.net will not restore individual files', and releases persist indefinitely (OpenOffice's mirror alone carries 166.4 MB files from 2015)

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Every release is 'automatically distributed to our worldwide network of download mirrors'. Downloads are served from per-mirror hostnames (zenlayer.dl / twds.dl / cfhcable.dl).sourceforge.net behind Cloudflare. Project Web states 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' and 'Our project web servers frequently handle more than 50M hits per day'.

record.tooling: Native SFTP, SCP, and rsync protocols are supported with documentation on the file release system page. Integrates with rclone via its native SFTP backend, and connects directly to restic, borg, or rsync. TCP port 22 to frs.sourceforge.net is open.
record.chaining: One account, many projects. Each project gets an independent tree at /home/frs/project/<unixname>/ and its own mirror distribution; one project admin can hold release-technician rights on many projects. Chained: (20-30 GB practical per project) x (N projects per account) x (N accounts). At 20 projects that is already 400-600 GB; the 10 GB/file mirror limit forces sharding, which is free because FRS is directory-based. Second chain: the same upload endpoint feeds project web space at /home/project-web/<unixname>/htdocs served as <unixname>.sourceforge.io, which is a separate quota-less static origin.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 10 GB per file. 'Individual files larger than 10 GB will not replicate out to our mirrors and can not be downloaded', so the only way past it is to shard. Request-rate: none published; upload is plain SFTP so it is limited by SSH session count, not an API quota. Retention: none. 'Users are responsible for backing up all of their files. SourceForge.net will not restore individual files', and releases persist indefinitely (OpenOffice's mirror alone carries 166.4 MB files from 2015). Reliability: signed mirror redirects are short-lived (see reliability_note).
record.reliability_note: Two real hazards found by probing. (1) The signed mirror URL from downloads.sourceforge.net 301s to a per-mirror host with an expiring token; You must re-resolve the redirect per session, or the mirror silently returns HTML. (2) There is no hard cap, which means the cap is discretionary — SourceForge mails 'over-quota' notices (the 2006 Inkscape notice shows a 100 MB soft quota on the shell/group dir) and can contact projects using 'significant storage'. Treat it as a soft ceiling that a human can raise or lower.
record.confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.

free_tier.stated: No quota stated anywhere on the page. The docs grant each project a vhost and say nothing about a byte limit. Practically it is the same filesystem family as FRS (uploaded over the same SFTP), so expect the same discretionary 20-30 GB band.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' (sourceforge.net/create). 'Our project web servers frequently handle more than 50M hits per day; we handle server scaling, caching, load balancing, and performance tuning.' Served through Cloudflare.

record.tooling: Same SFTP/SCP/rsync upload path as FRS but to /home/project-web/<unixname>/htdocs. Static files come back over plain HTTPS on <unixname>.sourceforge.io. No client, no API, just a web origin. Custom domains supported via the Custom VHOST service.
record.chaining: A second independent quota-less origin per project, free once you already have the project. Because it is a static web origin rather than a download mirror, it is the natural Cloudflare-fronted serving layer for anything in FRS: serves as the hot/serving tier while FRS holds the archive. N projects -> N vhosts.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: none published (it is a web root, not an artefact store). Request-rate: none published. Retention: 'always-on' service, files persist while the project exists. Practical caveat: it is a web root. Directory indexes are not guaranteed, so you index your own paths.
record.reliability_note: Probed live: https://libreoffice.sourceforge.io/ -> 200 with 134,123 bytes of real HTML; https://gimp.sourceforge.io/ -> 403 (project redirects elsewhere). https://gparted.sourceforge.io/ -> 302 to the project's own domain. Expect some projects to 403/302 depending on their custom-VHOST config; a fresh project should serve its own root.
